name: 0xdbdd45150249e229eB4c
headline: Takes liquidity during live games across ITF/ATP tennis, NBA, CS2, Dota 2 and college football. Its profit is real and recent, but no public-data rule reproduces its decisions: on ESPN-covered games it barely reacts to scoring plays, and most of its volume is in sports with no public timestamped event feed.
mechanism: All 200 sampled fills are taker fills (on-chain); 99.5% occur after game start; median fill $11; peak capital at risk $33k. Bought shares win more often than their price at 0.65-0.85 (e.g. paid 0.746, won 80.7%). On 128 ESPN-covered games there is no fill spike right after scoring plays (only a small bump 10-15 s after), and direction agreement after plays is 59% vs 55% for other takers.

roc.detail: peak capital at risk $33.4k; 30-day PnL $61.7k; 185% per month

match.detail: ESPN-covered games: direction 59% vs 55% for other takers (perm p=0.005, weak), no excess reaction (perm p=0.30); ~70% of volume is in tennis/esports/other with no public event feed to test against

backtest.detail: REACT(D=10s, W=120s) on 66 held-out games: +4.6%, per-game p=0.25; wallet's own fills on those games +8.2%, p=0.19

replicable.detail: decision inputs unknown; the testable public-data proxy is not significantly profitable

persistence.detail: last 30 days significant (p=0.004); no significant decline (p=0.12) or trend (p=0.81)

reasons: No reverse-engineered rule matches its decisions at the required significance; the scoring-play reaction is weak (59% vs 55%).
Most of its volume trades sports without a public timestamped event feed, so its signal cannot be reconstructed from public data.
The best public-data proxy is not significantly profitable on held-out games (p=0.25).
